children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on SoundHound AI

SoundHound AI’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 48 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock dropped 4% on the news that rising Treasury yields, hawkish Federal Reserve commentary, and broad de-risking hit the tech sector ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO.

Rate pressure intensified as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.145% after October retail sales excluding autos and gas rose 0.6%, topping the 0.4% consensus, CNBC reported. In remarks carried by CNBC, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned as many as four more rate hikes may be needed before spring 2027 to return inflation to 2%. Meanwhile, Bank of America's fund manager survey, detailed by CNBC, showed net overweight tech exposure fell 25 percentage points this month—the steepest drop since 2006—leaving strategist Michael Hartnett "tactically risk-off."

Higher borrowing costs compress software valuations, while Anthropic's upcoming listing gives institutions a direct public vehicle for AI exposure. Investors now look to Nvidia's post-close results and Anthropic's IPO pricing to test whether AI demand lifts or sidelines traditional software stocks.

SoundHound AI is down 75.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $2.62 per share, it is trading 79.6% below its 52-week high of $12.80 from December 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of SoundHound AI’s shares at the IPO in April 2022 would now be looking at an investment worth $348.67.
